newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close firmer amid improved U.S. tone.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close firmer amid improved U.S. tone.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed slightly firmer on Thursday, boosted by a more positive tone in U.S. treasuries and subdued U.S. economic data this morning, analysts said.
"I think we're definitely taking our lead from the U.S. market today," said Rich Wylie, a fixed-income economist with TD Securities Inc. "We saw some very weak retail sales numbers in the U.S."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.03 to C$110.35 to yield 7.125 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.63 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds was 50 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Wednesday.

Canadian and U.S. bonds strengthened this morning following reports that U.S. retail sales for November fell by 0.4 percent from October. Economists had expected a 0.3 percent rise. A second report showing consumer price increases remained subdued also benefitted markets.
The positive data followed a sharp selloff of Canadian and U.S. bonds on Wednesday, when speculation that Japanese investors will ease up on purchases of North American bonds drove prices lower.
Analysts said many portfolio managers are now hesitant to take large positions in the market, given recent volatility, and the fact that the year end is near.

"I think the incentive for people on the Canadian side is to be relatively flat. I don't think they want do an awful lot of buying or selling before year end," said Joe Lee, a portfolio manager with Laketon Investment Management.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.22 to C$103.65 to yield 6.496 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 2/32 to yield 6.38 percent.
The spread between the bonds widened to 12 basis points from 11 basis points at Wednesday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.96 percent against the U.S. bill at 4.95 percent.
